title: Modules & Mixins
intro: Ruby uses modules in place of multiple inheritance, and understanding exactly how include, extend, and prepend each affect the method lookup chain is a mandatory interview topic at any serious Rails shop. Include inserts the module above the class in the ancestors chain; extend adds the module's methods as singleton methods; prepend inserts the module before the class, enabling method wrapping without monkey-patching. This page covers all three, plus the two most powerful standard mixins: Enumerable (implement each, get the entire collection API for free) and Comparable (implement <=>, get all comparison operators). Every answer explains the MRO impact so you can reason about method dispatch, not just recite the difference.
